clue.text: Tour boring little American shopping centre

indicators.note: boring here means drilling through, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: little means small
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A trip that bores a small American is spent trailing round a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' belongs with the wordplay, not with 'American'; the definition is only 'American shopping centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of shops along a roadside with shared parking is the usual US name for a modest retail precinct.

clue.text: Son on Caribbean island getting breathing apparatus

parts.note: Cuba is the largest Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A boy on a Caribbean holiday is fitted with diving gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus names a diver's air tank set.

clue.text: Beneficiary of surprisingly nice trip around Spain

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters are wrapped about the country's code
surprisingly hints the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone is the lucky winner of a pleasant trip round Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who receives a gift or award is the one who benefits.

clue.text: A model's abnormal sexual desire

parts.note: 'a' can mean per, as in five pounds a head
a model of a car or gadget is a version

explanation.surface: A fashion model is said to have unusual tastes in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' as PER is the sense in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deviation from what is considered normal sexual behaviour is the older clinical sense of this word.

clue.text: German Christian snubbing Charlie

indicators.note: snubbing means leaving out, so the letter is cold-shouldered from the word

parts.note: an Anglican is a Christian of the Church of England
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A German churchgoer ignores someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbing' drops the C from ANGLICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic tribe, so belonging to them is, loosely, Germanic.

clue.text: Overdue entering records? They must be displayed before passing

definitions.text: They must be displayed before passing

indicators.note: entering means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Late returns of records must be on show before they go out again.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows red-on-white L signs until passing the driving test.
explanation.definitionFit: Learner drivers in the UK must show these signs on the car until passing the test.

clue.text: University official cut right-hand page

indicators.note: cut means the official's title is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a rector heads some universities, notably in Scotland

explanation.surface: A university administrator trims a page of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last R of RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the front of a leaf, read on the right of an open book, has this Latin-derived technical name.

clue.text: Study sound made by grass

indicators.note: sound made by points to a word that is pronounced the same as another

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

explanation.surface: Researching the noise grass makes in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound made by' signals a homophone of REED.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at university, as in 'she studied law', is a British use of this verb.

clue.text: Tea bags popular for teacups?

indicators.note: bags means holds or encloses, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Tea bags are the popular choice for filling teacups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' reads as one noun, but 'bags' is a verb meaning holds. CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain tableware, such as cups and saucers, collectively goes by this name.

clue.text: Dreadful toy shaver produces rash

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A cheap toy razor gives someone a shaving rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' poses as a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting too quickly, without due thought, is reckless or rash.

clue.text: Cryptic clue originally rejected for sore

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, telling us to scramble the letters
originally points to the first letter of the word rejected

explanation.surface: A crossword clue was rejected because it was a sore point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' rearranges CLUE plus R, the start of 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open lesion on skin or a mucous membrane is a synonym for a sore.

clue.text: Stimulate a Svengali to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the following words must alter their order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to rouse a manipulative mentor into reforming.
explanation.walkthrough: A Svengali is a manipulative controlling figure, from the hypnotist in Du Maurier's Trilby; 'to change' shuffles A SVENGALI.
explanation.definitionFit: To jolt into action, originally by electric current, is to stimulate someone.

clue.text: Relish rise in value

definitions.meaning: to relish something is to enjoy and value it
assets such as property gain worth over time

explanation.surface: Enjoy watching your investments grow.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both savouring something and increasing in market worth.

clue.text: Frustrate — bother!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of mild annoyance, like 'drat!'

explanation.surface: An irritated exclamation at being thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes can be dashed, i.e. thwarted, and 'Dash it!' is a mild old-fashioned oath.

clue.text: Voyage in haste

definitions.meaning: a long journey for a purpose, such as exploring
speed and promptness in doing something

explanation.surface: A sea journey made in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both an organised journey and, formally, speed or promptness.

clue.text: Bit of tame excuse for betraying one's country

indicators.note: a bit of the word tame here is just its opening letter

parts.note: an excuse is a reason given

explanation.surface: A feeble excuse offered for selling out one's nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of betraying one's own state, as by aiding its enemies, is this offence.

clue.text: Passing agnostic oddly bathed in Midlands river

indicators.note: bathed in means the letters are immersed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent flows through the English Midlands

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of agnostic

explanation.surface: A passing doubter takes a dip in a river in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like part of the surface but is the definition, in its sense of fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief and short-lived, staying only a while, is fleeting.

clue.text: It is beginning to trigger southern bigots

parts.note: 'it' is a coy old word for sex appeal or sex

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the word trigger

explanation.surface: Something is starting to set off prejudiced people from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex is a crossword staple, from Kipling's and Clara Bow's 'It'.
explanation.definitionFit: People prejudiced against one gender are a particular kind of bigot.

clue.text: South American footballer Ronaldo mostly ignoring current church official

indicators.note: ignoring means a further letter is left out of the name
mostly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Cristiano Ronaldo is the Portuguese footballer
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A footballer is said to ignore the current church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks CRISTIANO to CRISTIAN; 'ignoring' then drops its I, giving CRISTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A church officer who looks after the vestry, vestments and sacred vessels holds this post.

clue.text: Accomplishments of leaderless rebellious groups

indicators.note: leaderless means the groups lose their front letter

parts.note: factions are dissenting groups within a body

explanation.surface: What rebel groups without a leader manage to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the F of FACTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds or things done can loosely be called accomplishments.

clue.text: Soon upset with rap singer

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer is soon upset by rap music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SOON and RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the highest female or boy's voice is one kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Inadequate, periodically knelt in school yard

indicators.note: in places the chosen letters inside the abbreviation for school
periodically takes every other letter of knelt

explanation.surface: A pupil kneeling now and then in the school yard does an inadequate job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school yard' looks like one place, but the two words give separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only roughed out and lacking detail is thin or insufficient.

clue.text: Observe we had picked up marine algae

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: observe is see, and we had contracts to we'd

explanation.surface: We noticed we had collected some ocean plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' means heard: 'see we'd' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp, wrack and other plants of the sea are large algae.

clue.text: Fifty in total hovel

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for total

parts.note: a total is a sum
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people crammed into one wretched shack.
explanation.definitionFit: A squalid, run-down dwelling or district is a broad equivalent of a hovel.

clue.text: Article taken away from dirty relative

indicators.note: taken away from means the article's letters are removed from the other word

parts.note: dirty means unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item is removed from a grubby family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken away from' removes AN from UNCLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, i.e. a relative.

clue.text: Piano part I played in Spectre

indicators.note: played suggests the words are performed in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A pianist performs a section of music in the Bond film Spectre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' shuffles PIANO PART I.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly figure appearing to someone is a phantom or spectre.

clue.text: Not a soul expected, initially, after midday

indicators.note: after says the letter comes behind the word for midday

parts.note: noon is midday

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of expected

explanation.surface: Nobody was expected to turn up after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying nobody at all is present is the same as saying not a single person.

clue.text: Kitty's enjoyable day

parts.note: fun means enjoyable

explanation.surface: A cat named Kitty has a pleasant day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a cat but is a pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money collected for a purpose is called a kitty.

clue.text: Persuade retinue to replace Tesla with Cadillac at last

indicators.note: to replace ... with signals swapping one letter in the word for another

parts.note: a retinue is an entourage of attendants
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of Cadillac

explanation.surface: A celebrity's retinue is persuaded to swap their Tesla car for a Cadillac.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla and Cadillac pose as car brands; the T in ENTOURAGE becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or embolden someone towards an action is to persuade or spur them on.

clue.text: Prelude from Fortnite rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the extracted letters are thrown back, read right to left
from tells us the letters are taken out of the word Fortnite

explanation.surface: An opening sequence cut out of the video game Fortnite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes ORTNI out of Fortnite; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory passage at the start of a song or show is a short informal word for a prelude.

clue.text: Flower close to ornament, unwanted plant

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word ornament

parts.note: a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted

explanation.surface: A flower near a garden ornament turns out to be a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows: a river. The Tweed runs along the Scotland–England border.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a crossword 'flower', a thing that flows, and this one marks the Anglo-Scottish border.

clue.text: One blocking weapons regulation

indicators.note: blocking means the numeral stands in the middle of the other word, like an obstruction

parts.note: ordnance is military weapons and artillery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single rule bans the carrying of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts I into ORDNANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A local by-law or authoritative decree is a form of regulation.
